record.original_question: Show that a typical L2 geodesic in D_mu^s(M) has absolute complexity growing linearly in time.

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Show that for a typical geodesic γ(t) in Dµs (M ) we have C(γ(t)) ≃ t. Roughly, we say that a family of geodesics starting from the identity in Dµs (M ) is typical if the complement of the corresponding set of initial velocities in Te Dµs has infinite codimension. Examples of “typical” L2 geodesics whose complexity grows linearly in time are the one-parameter subgroups of Dµs (M ) and (possibly) the quasi-periodic solutions of (1.1).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold (possibly with boundary) equipped with a smooth Riemannian volume form $\mu$. For a real Sobolev exponent $s>\dim(M)/2+1$, let $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ denote the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ of Sobolev class $H^s$. This group is a smooth infinite-dimensional Hilbert manifold; its tangent space at the identity $e$ is
$$T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)=\{u\in H^s(TM):\operatorname{div}_\mu u=0,\ u\parallel\partial M\}.$$
Equip $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ with the right-invariant $L^2$ metric
$$\langle U,V\rangle_\eta=\int_M \langle U(x),V(x)\rangle_{g(\eta(x))}\,d\mu(x),\qquad U,V\in T_\eta\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M).$$
Geodesics $\eta(t)\in\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ of this metric starting at $e$ correspond, via $u(t)=\dot\eta(t)\circ\eta(t)^{-1}$, to solutions of the incompressible Euler equations
$$\partial_t u+\nabla_u u=-\nabla p,\qquad \operatorname{div} u=0.$$

For a Lagrangian path $\gamma:[0,T]\to \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ with $\gamma(0)=e$, define the absolute complexity $C(\gamma(t))$ as the (suitably normalized) length of the shortest path in $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ joining $e$ to $\gamma(t)$ in the right-invariant $L^2$ metric, i.e.
$$C(\gamma(t))=\operatorname{dist}_{L^2}(e,\gamma(t)).$$

Call a family of geodesics in $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ starting at $e$ \emph{typical} if the complement, in $T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$, of the set of their initial velocities has infinite codimension.

Problem. Prove that for a typical $L^2$ geodesic $\gamma(t)$ in $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ one has
$$C(\gamma(t))\asymp t\qquad\text{as }t\to\infty,$$
i.e.\ the absolute complexity grows linearly in time.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in a 2023 survey on the geometry of diffeomorphism groups. No subsequent work appears to establish the linear-in-time growth of absolute complexity for typical L2 geodesics on the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group; one-parameter subgroups and (conjecturally) quasi-periodic solutions are only known examples.
